title: How Iman Gadzhi went from broke teen to $100M: five years running a social media agency
summary: A year-by-year documentary of Iman's agency journey from a £95/week first client in 2016 to millions by 21. It covers pricing lessons (retainers plus performance fees, lifetime value over monthly price), sales habits, hiring mistakes, and investing agency cash flow rather than letting it sit idle.

principles.text: Optimize for client lifetime value, not monthly price: lower retainers kept longer beat high retainers that churn fast.
principles.quote: it's much better to have a clan that pays $25,000 a month and you keep them for 10 months rather than a clan that pays $5,000 a month and you only keep them for 3 months

principles.text: Charge a lower base retainer plus a performance fee, with longer minimum terms, to earn far more per client.
principles.quote: we would have much lower base retainers but because of our performance that we were delivering for our clients you know we were still building way more than five figures a month

principles.text: Never work with an agency that charges a percentage of ad spend or revenue, because incentives must be aligned.
principles.quote: if an agency ever charges you percentage of AD spend or percentage of Revenue just leave the meeting because here's the issue okay our incentives need to be aligned

principles.text: Price per client based on value and work involved, and don't sell packages without diagnosing the client's problem first.
principles.quote: I always tell people like don't do packages don't do packages and also your pricing should be different per client

principles.text: Don't qualify yourself to high-level people; act like you belong from the start of the conversation.
principles.quote: you act like you're here from the get-go it's a lot better of a dynamic to start the uh start the meeting off in that Way

principles.text: Agencies are cash-flow machines; send profits into an investment portfolio monthly and let compounding work.
principles.quote: when you have cash flow you invest it and then you let the compounding nature of time do its trick
